subjects.displayTitle: Publication and review: accuracy, encouragement, and responsibility
subjects.introduction: Every book carries a voice beyond the reach of the one who spoke, and what travels with it may be the exact words, a translator’s improvements, or an impression nobody checked. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá treats this as a matter of trust. He welcomes the gathering of His talks and insists they be exact, asks that a treatise be softened so that no reader is hurt, has a printed Aqdas compared against a trusted manuscript, and admits that even an address can carry a secretary’s slip. The same hand that corrects a friend’s poetry amid a hundred thousand occupations praises an article as the crown of all works, which suggests that encouragement and exacting revision belong together. Permissions to print, pauses in restless cities, secrecy in times of arrest, and replies to a disputed history each answer a particular moment, and Shoghi Effendi later calls review a provisional measure for a young community, rooted in the individual’s right to speak from conscience and in frank and loving consultation. Proverbs counsels hearing before answering and testing a first persuasive account, a habit of mind rather than a procedure. The inquiry opens outward into the meaning of wisdom, into newspapers and the media, and into the balance between defending and protecting the Cause.
subjects.arc: Begin with fidelity to a speaker’s words and care for the reader; examine textual checking and translation; follow encouragement into practical publishing and consultation; read disputed histories and protective measures in context; close with expression, responsibility and the purpose of review.

order.why: Open with the responsibility to preserve exact talks without a translator’s alterations.
shortened: Your collection of 'Abdu'l-Baha's talks which you intend to publish is very appropriate. This service will cause your face to shine in the Abha Kingdom and make you the object of praise and gratitude among the friends of East and West. However, utmost care must be taken that they are the exact talks and that no alterations have been made by previous translators.

order.why: Ask revision to protect and enlarge the reader’s heart.
Read the reported purpose of a publication through hope and illumination.
shortened: A Baha'i publication must never publish anything which may cause provocations or injure the feelings of any one or displease any soul. It must publish such matters that would be conducive to the happiness, hopefulness, advancement, guidance and illumination of the readers.

order.why: Imagine a library open to seekers as the result of responsible publishing.
Place the writer’s health and peace of heart beside the desired completion of a book.
shortened: O thou whom God hath aided with hosts from the Concourse on High!
Your noble letter with its gracious contents brought boundless joy and delight, for it indicated that your health is moderate and the conclusive book is nearing completion.
If the book were completed during winter and you could travel to Tehran in spring it would be most suitable, but your comfort and peace of heart are foremost to me above all else.

order.why: Distinguish changes of wording from changes of meaning.
Introduce verification before acting on an unsigned letter.
shortened: You had inquired about the despatched and unsigned letter. That letter is authentic and its original copy is safely kept and signed. Whenever an unsigned letter arrives, inquire before putting in into action and wait until an answer is given.

order.why: Compare a printed text with a trusted manuscript.
shortened: Compare the Kitab-i-Aqdas with the handwriting of him who attained the presence of his Lord, His Holiness Zaynu'l-Muqarrabin, upon him be the Glory of God. The printed version produced under the interference of the Center of Violation is not correct; the handwriting of Jinab-i-Zayn is accurate.

order.why: Read the acknowledgment that even addresses can contain secretarial errors.
Ask when a difference of meaning calls for inquiry.
shortened: And should there arise any difference regarding the meaning of any of the divine utterances or verses that have been sent down, inquire so that the purpose may become clear to all.

order.why: Join careful review with eloquence in translation.
Consider both script and the need for a group of skilled translators.
shortened: As for what you wrote about scripts, the Nasta'liq script is very acceptable. Therefore, if efforts are made to produce printing type in Nasta'liq script, that would be most suitable. Regarding the translation of the Kitab-i-Aqdas, no single person can translate it. A group skilled in both the foreign language and Arabic must translate it with utmost care.

order.why: Keep the reported insistence on a capable translation before issuing the Aqdas.
Read the proposed translation priorities and the requirement to match texts carefully.
shortened: And Mr. Hishmatullah should engage in translating important Tablets that are relevant to these days and contain teachings on the oneness of humanity, universal peace, investigation of truth, uniting hearts through the power of religion, reconciliation of science and religion, abandonment of vain prejudices, establishment of the Supreme Tribunal, justice between women and men, universalization of education, invention of a universal language, work and crafts being worship, limiting jihad to the tongue and utterance, and so forth - and they should be carefully matched and published.

order.why: Preserve the particular rejection of Kheirella’s translations in its source setting.
Read the correction of erroneous copies alongside the call to publish sacred texts.
Keep the short notice of a corrected copy being sent.
Consider a requested addition to the second edition of Phelps’s book.
Read the waiting for collation and translation of Some Answered Questions.
Keep the permission to publish talks after collection and correction.
Read the reported wish to gather scattered American addresses.
Retain the reported clarification that advance submission concerns newcomers.
shortened: There may be speaking from a text taken from the writings, but it should be written out by the speakers and three days before the meeting be submitted to the believers for approval.
The provision of submitting a paper before it shall be read at a meeting refers to newcomers, not to regular speakers at the meeting. It is to guard against chatterboxes.

order.why: Bring historical knowledge into the review of articles.
Compare conflicting narratives before assembling a history.
Notice the midnight reading and request for missing pages.
Keep the diarist’s description of corrections as a narrated scene.
Read the careful personal review of an Arabic translation about Tahirih.
Keep the separate approval of a translated pamphlet and a reply.
Notice the modest extent of revision before publication.
Read the invitation to review translated pages in an Assembly.
Preserve the request to send a particular translation for review.
Let pleasure in a poem coexist with revision.
Read the labor of correcting poetry as guidance for future writing.
shortened: Consider how intensely the fire of this servant's love for you burns, that despite a hundred thousand occupations and lack of time, I undertook to correct your poetry so that it may serve as a model for the future of his honor Qabil, and whatever he may sing in the arts of melody upon the branches of utterance may be in this station and tune, that it may be chanted in the gatherings of the Kingdom and assemblies of the Realm of Might, nay even in the monasteries of the Realm of Divinity, and its melody may reach the ears of the Guardian of the Most Glorious Kingdom and become the manifestation of praise.

order.why: Keep the stated concern that poetry express servitude to Baha.
Retain the particular encouragement to correct a first book.
Read the request to help correct another author’s book.
shortened: Concerning the correction of the book of that Christian person, shouldst thou be successful in this matter, it would be a great achievement, and a most necessary one. If and when he writeth the book he now hath in mind, let him then bring it with him.

order.why: Keep the account of attraction and inspiration in composition.
shortened: At the time of writing the power of attraction was manifest and apparent and the real teacher was instructing and inspiring: Consequently it was composed in the utmost fluency and eloquence.

order.why: Read the verse’s eloquence alongside the hope of attracting hearts.
Preserve the presentation of Andalib’s poetry and prose.
Consider a book’s counsels, morals and power to awaken.
Ask how a brief treatise may contain a detailed exposition.
Read the reported preference for books with logical and spiritual arguments.
shortened: In this day, the most useful books are those which demonstrate the validity of the Cause with logical proofs, intellectual evidences and spiritual arguments.

order.why: Consider the proposed journal’s public emphasis on teachings and unity.
Let brevity, sweetness and verbatim quotation guide an article.
shortened: The translation of Tablets is acceptable and beloved. If, occasionally, thou writest a concise, terse and useful article, with the utmost sweetness, containing the teachings and exhortations of the Blessed Perfection, verbatim, for the purpose of publishing in the journals of Denmark, it will be most agreeable.

order.why: Read the journal as a mirror of truth.
shortened: Indeed, your unique journal is like a pure and delicate mirror in which images of truth are reflected. It is the manifestation of truth that appears in this journal, and all Baha'is are grateful and pleased with your good intentions.

order.why: Keep the distinct mirror image for the Star of the West.
Preserve the letter’s praise and expectations for an article in their source setting.
shortened: I am very grateful and pleased with you, especially regarding your fair and truth-nurturing article published in The Christian Commonwealth. Indeed, until now no one has written such an article, and from the pen of European authors no such pure and unblemished work about the Cause of Baha'u'llah has appeared.

order.why: Read the further comparison between earthly and heavenly works as encouragement.
shortened: There is no doubt that thou hast written this article through the Confirmations of the Kingdom, because most of its contents indicated the assistance of the invisible Inspirations.

There are many authors and their written works are circulated in all parts of the world but this article of thine is the crown of all the works, because the works of others deal with the material world while this composition belongs to the world of the Kingdom. They are earthly melodies but this is a heavenly harmony.

order.why: Keep the reported prospect of books studied by future generations.
Let the rose-garden image express anticipation before a book arrives.
shortened: O promoter of the religion of God! Although the New Journey has not yet arrived, since that excellent book is a rose garden of divine truths and meanings, and contains the glad tidings of the divine Prophets, therefore its sweet fragrance has reached our nostrils before its arrival.

order.why: Distinguish the friends’ praise from the writer’s own future reading.
shortened: O son of the Kingdom!
The book which you had written and sent has arrived, and the friends are busy reading it and highly praise and commend your book. God willing, when it is translated I will read it too.

order.why: Keep the encouragement for Isabella’s book and dramas.
Retain the concise invitation to write a contemplated book.
shortened: Say to the beloved maid-servant of God, ..., to write the book which she had in mind.

order.why: Read the named book project with its encouragement to persist.
shortened: Give thanks unto God for this and strive to compose the book "The Proof of the Manifestation of the All-Merciful from the Dawning-Place of Possibility." The breathings of the Holy Spirit will assist thee in this at all times and moments.

order.why: Acknowledge the work already done on twelve chapters.
Follow praise of a composition toward translation and publication.
shortened: He gives the highest praise and description of your new composition, saying its publication and distribution would be extremely beneficial. Therefore through the efforts of His Holiness Maknat its eloquent translation must be completed with all speed and published.

order.why: Read the welcome for the compilation of Sadru’s-Sudur’s proofs.
shortened: And regarding the book of proofs by Sadru's-Sudur and its compilation and arrangement that you wrote about, we were extremely pleased. Send that book to the Holy Shrine so it can later be printed and published.

order.why: Give collective organization a role in preserving a writer’s unfinished labor.
shortened: I sent these to Tehran so that you, along with Jinab-i-Na'im, Jinab-i-Ibn-i-Abhar, Jinab-i-Ibn-i-Asdaq, Jinab-i-Mulla Muhammad-'Ali-i-Qa'ini, Jinab-i-Samandar, and Jinab-i-Aqa Siyyid Mahdi (son of that noble one's sister) may arrange a gathering that maintains the utmost order and organization, and from those blessed papers extract one book or two books or multiple treatises for publication, so that noble one's efforts are not wasted.

order.why: Keep the separate instruction to extract treatises from Abu’l-Fadl’s papers.
Connect printing with preventing an author’s work from being lost.
Notice the readers waiting for a book’s appearance.
shortened: Regarding the book, please write what stage it has reached, for hearts are awaiting its issuance.

order.why: Read the pleasure of an earlier volume and anticipation of its sequel.
shortened: The book that you sent last year was printed in Tehran in very beautiful calligraphy and was distributed throughout Iran. Everyone read it day and night with utmost joy and delight, and all are awaiting the second volume as promised, but due to preoccupations it has not yet appeared.

order.why: Keep the approval of Abu’l-Fadl’s book and another Hidden Words edition.
shortened: Thou hast written that the publication of the book of Mirza Abuil Fazl is commenced. This is very acceptable, for his books are written with the utmost sincerity. Likewise the translation of the Hidden Words that you are just thinking to print another edition, this is also acceptable.

order.why: Retain the brief acknowledgment of a received Mathnavi.
shortened: The Book of Mathnavi was received and in time it will be published.

order.why: Read the separate permissions concerning narratives and teaching books.
Keep the approval of the history of the Yazd martyrs.
Preserve the short call to promote proofs and martyr histories.
Read the translated Traveller’s Narrative as a brief resource for distribution.
Consider the Paris Talks translation through the image of a raised banner.
shortened: The book containing the translation of the Paris Talks has arrived. Thou hast indeed labored arduously. God willing, it will become the cause of the spread of the Cause in those regions. This translation is like a banner that has been raised. It will surely yield momentous results.

order.why: Keep the proposed translations through Guthrie and Gibran.
Read the reported invitation to Ali-Kuli Khan to assist by translating.
shortened: You have come to assist me by translating His Sacred Writings as well as my letters to the friends in America and elsewhere in the West...

order.why: Retain the specific request for an eloquent translation of an enclosed letter.
Keep the practical instruction to translate Stuttgart letters for their owners.
Read the reported book project interrupted by death.
Consider the reported call to enlarge publishing across languages and capacities.
shortened: "In a similar manner the scope of the Bahai Publishing Society must be greatly enlarged, so that books and pamphlets may be translated into different languages and published. These short pamphlets and historical reviews, giving the proofs and arguments of the Cause, must be written in accordance with the intellectual and spiritual capacity of each people.

order.why: Begin distribution from the reader’s work of study.
Keep the presentation of selected writings to the British Library.
Read the sending of the Epistle to the Son of the Wolf to Paris.
shortened: The Blessed Book which is addressed to the Wolf was sent to Paris through the efforts of Jinab-i-Mirza Haji Aqa through your intermediary. This was a source of great joy.

order.why: Preserve the notice of two senders’ books arriving in Paris.
Keep the list of books approved for presentation to particular people.
Compare a different selection recommended for a particular historian.
Read the differing timing of English, French and Persian editions in its context.
Keep the permission to print and circulate the Iqan.
shortened: Regarding the Kitab-i-Iqan, it was previously written that its printing and distribution among the friends is appropriate and suitable.

order.why: Read the encouragement concerning the Treatise on Civilization.
Preserve the permission to publish the economics Tablet in an American journal.
Keep the emphasis on placing a particular article in major newspapers.
shortened: I have written for thy sake the Message that thou hast requested. Endeavor thou that this Article may appear in the London Times. If this is impossible, i.e., its publication in the columns of the Times, then publish it by all means in other important periodicals or journals. This question along with this article is very important. Display ye the utmost effort in its publication.

order.why: Consider the decision to publish original and translation together in a separate treatise.
Preserve the specific instruction to separate sacred writings from a present book list.
Keep the instruction regarding proofs already printed with the Hidden Words.
Read approval of the two treatises in different languages.
Retain encouragement to publish with the friends’ assistance.
shortened: And as for the treatise you had written - publish and distribute this treatise. The friends of God will certainly assist you in publishing this treatise.

order.why: Keep the permission after revision and refinement of a treatise on unity.
Read approval of the short Service in the Kingdom treatise.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the Covenant!
The short treatise which thou hast written upon "Service in the Kingdom," forwarding it here and asking permission for its publication, was read. Spread it among the believers.

order.why: Distinguish limited reading from the particular permission granted.
shortened: Regarding the book you asked about, although I never have time to read, nevertheless I read a few pages. It contained mention of the Blessed Beauty, therefore you have permission to publish it.

order.why: Acknowledge effort in publishing Tablets.
Attend to the quality of printing and handwriting.
Keep the approval of translating and photographing Tablets.
Read the particular permission for a photograph of the Blessed House.
Consider photographs as evidence of historic sites and early believers.
Bring preservation, copying and the absence of a bookbinder into view.
Let envelopes become carriers of wisdom in the source’s imagery.
Read the practical limits on preparing specimens of handwriting.
Notice the printing press and photographic equipment needed for a request.
shortened: But it would have been necessary for them to also send a printing press from Paris or a photographic apparatus from England - then perhaps one could fulfill this request.

order.why: Keep the further printing-press comparison about the volume of letters.
Attend to the work of two secretaries and the writer’s own hand.
shortened: Two secretaries, Mirza Nuru'd-Din and Mirza Mahmud-i-Zarqani, are constantly writing and cannot keep up, and I myself am continuously writing with my own pen. Despite this, I cannot keep up, and due to the volume of writing I do not leave the house and have not a moment's rest or comfort.

order.why: Preserve the admission of insufficient time for weekly commentary.
shortened: And I too must write a detailed commentary every week and have absolutely no time, nor am I in a state to occupy myself with such matters.

order.why: Read the limited time for reviewing journal copies.
shortened: Copies of the journal were received through His Honor Aqa Mirza Mehdi, but due to the press of duties it was only possible to immediately review one copy. God willing the other copies will also be read in succession and if anything needs to be written it will be written.

order.why: Join delayed reading with the general instruction for Assembly approval.
Keep the request for copies when none could be retained locally.
Read the concern about letters delayed in transit.
shortened: O Jinab-i-Aqa Siyyid Asadu'llah! Letters arrive and remain with you for several days. Among them, Mirza Jalal had sent a letter, but after he himself arrived, his letter reached us. Please be attentive in this matter.

order.why: Preserve the account of opening enclosures with permission.
Keep the notice of letters presented with other petitions.
Read the correction of an omission in sending two Tablets.
Retain the promised dispatch of a recently revealed Tablet.
shortened: A few days ago a Tablet was graciously revealed specifically for him. God willing, after this, along with the reply to his letter, this evanescent servant will write and send it.

order.why: Keep the concise statement about the specifically revealed response.
Preserve the particular instruction to wait for an utterance.
Read the separate sending of Aqdas ordinances in answer to questions.
Keep the exchange concerning a requested book and a supplied list.
Read the Bab’s request to carry copies to the faithful.
shortened: Make mention in the Book of Isma'il, that thou shouldst carry some copies and deliver them unto God's faithful servants.

order.why: Consider prompt copying so a messenger is not delayed.
Keep the proposed circulation of a Persian Tablet across regions.
shortened: The Persian Tablet that was revealed specifically for the friends in the Land of Qaf - it would be good if copies reach the Land of Ta and other regions.

order.why: Retain the permission to send passages named Traveler to Europe.
Read the particular provision for adding recipients’ names.
shortened: Another submission: Some copies of the Most Holy, Most Glorious Tablet of Javad were sent in the revealed handwriting without names. They may write the name of whomever they deem advisable and give it to them.

order.why: Notice the request to deliver books as demand grows.
shortened: Those who repose upon the carpet of oneness, and who are seated in the court of love, and who recline upon the cushions of eternity, and who gaze upon the Countenance of the Ancient of Days - unto all of them do I convey my greetings and salutations, and unto you especially do I express them, and trouble you that you should definitely make every effort to deliver the books, as many customers have appeared.

order.why: Keep the practical arrangement for postal delivery from Egypt.
shortened: It will be written to Egypt that books should be sent by post.

order.why: Read advance subscriptions as material support for a newspaper.
Keep the continuity of publishing during interrupted communications.
shortened: You had written that throughout the period of communications being cut off, you were engaged in service, publishing and distributing books, and that the Star of the West was also being published and regularly distributed.
Send a copy of that book to the Holy Land.

order.why: Preserve the careful instructions to send newspapers in envelopes.
Let a translated account carry the attraction of Western friends eastward.
Retain the report of a detailed letter printed in Tehran.
Keep the request to translate and circulate a newspaper article with a report.
shortened: Have the newspaper article translated and printed together with a copy of the report, and disseminate them in other directions.

order.why: Consider circulation that helps readers reflect on conduct.
Read the use of notes to encourage construction of the Temple.
Keep the request to print a handwritten Tablet in the Star of the West.
Read the careful handwriting of a general letter before wide circulation.
shortened: Therefore, a general letter has been written and is being sent, so that you may transcribe it in very fine handwriting, print it, and send it to all regions.

order.why: Preserve the specific request for forty or fifty copies.
Keep the instruction to circulate Mirza Ahmad’s letter.
Retain the notice that papers for publication will be sent.
Keep the particular response intended for printing and distribution.
shortened: A response regarding this matter was written and sent so that you may print it and distribute it among the friends.

order.why: Let the brief call for prompt distribution stand distinctly.
Distinguish a book awaiting review from letters explicitly marked for circulation.
Keep the request to prepare booklets before an arrival.
Read title-page simplicity and the Assembly’s majority decision.
Consider local responsibility for publishing talks given in a city.
shortened: The publication of 'Abdu'l-Baha's talks in any city is up to the opinion of the friends in that city. For example, the talks that were given in Washington are up to the opinion of the Spiritual Assembly of that city. If they wish, they can collect, publish and distribute them in Washington itself, but other cities have no involvement in this.

order.why: Keep the Assembly’s discretion concerning appropriate sacred writings.
shortened: Some of the sacred writings that the Spiritual Assembly deems appropriate may be published.

order.why: Read the stated purpose of committee review: order and factual care.
Preserve the separate requirement of the Executive Committee’s judgment.
Keep the reported sequence involving convention and committee.
Read a particular title-page statement as dependent on prior examination.
Retain the request to send a proposed book before publication.
Requires committee examination before the printing and circulation of new publications.
Keep the explicit condition of review for Proofs of the Covenant.
shortened: Send the book Proofs of the Covenant that you have authored so that I may review it and return it. This way is better and you should definitely not publish it without my review.

order.why: Read the general requirement to send writings to the Holy Land in its historical setting.
Preserve the cable’s explanation of its general scope across regions.
Keep the proposed six-month rhythm for a magazine and its correction.
shortened: Thou hast written regarding the publication of a magazine. If thou shouldst edit one magazine every six months--two in a year--then forward it to the Holy Land to be corrected and returned, after due correction, for its publication--it is very acceptable will be the cause of the penetration of the Word of God. [...]

order.why: Retain the concise warning about difficulties from unconfirmed publications.
shortened: New York, Mr. Dodge and other friends: Unconfirmed publications are absolutely not permitted. The resulting difficulties are too numerous.

order.why: Read the separate requirement concerning writings about the Cause with its omission.
Keep the brief statement concerning authorization.
Read government permission within the letter’s stated context.
Preserve the response to a particular unauthorized Aqdas printing.
shortened: It has become known that the Kitab-i-Aqdas was published without government permission, and this contradicts the decisive divine text. The perpetrator must surely repent and seek forgiveness. If any book is published without the permission and authorization of the government, it is not permissible for any of the friends of God to purchase it.

order.why: Keep the distinct and forceful explanation of obedience in that case.
Read the reported inclusion of printing among matters for discussion.
Join accurate copies with care about surrounding consequences.
Read consultation and limits on printing amid the danger of unrest.
shortened: Regarding what you mentioned about the printing of the Book, this matter is contingent upon consultation. In these days, wisdom dictates against printing, for should the sacred revealed Books proliferate in that city, it would surely provoke an outcry from the ignorant of the earth. Though beneficial for those possessed of true vision and spiritual hearing, such souls are few in number in any city, while most would rise up crying "O the religion!" without thought or consideration of consequences.

order.why: Distinguish compiling a fine manuscript from publishing it at that time.
shortened: Concerning the compilation of Divine Tablets specifically addressed to you, this is very good and appropriate, but printing and publication is absolutely inappropriate at present, as many people would be inclined toward this and difficulties would arise therefrom. However, you may compile one copy in very fine handwriting and send it to me.

order.why: Keep the postponement of a publishing company during war.
shortened: You had written about Mr. Herborn's desire to establish a company for the publication and dissemination of the divine teachings. At present this is not advisable, as it is wartime. But God willing, this war will end in peace; afterward we shall meet with him and make firm arrangements in this regard.

order.why: Read the particular distinction between study among friends and public circulation.
Preserve the preference for general rather than specific treatises.
Keep the concern about books admitted to a school in its setting.
Retain the brief restriction on giving a particular treatise to outsiders.
Keep the particular instruction to circulate without a named author.
Read the request to protect the identities of particular people.
shortened: Keep extremely confidential such important persons as the honored Astarabadi and the esteemed person from Khurasan, and maintain their secrecy. Do not mention them even to those who are privy to secrets.

order.why: Keep the preservation and concealment of Tablets connected to actual arrests.
shortened: Great effort must be made to preserve the Tablets and Divine verses. It seems some have been negligent in this matter, as evidenced by the fact that when some friends were arrested in certain lands, their writings were discovered before they themselves were apprehended. In any case, mention of the Land of the Prison, as well as the Tablets, must remain concealed. Complete concealment is what behooveth us, and He is the Preserver, the Helper, the Mighty, the Great.

order.why: Read the warning about hostile investigators in its historical setting.
Preserve the condition of confidence before giving the specified book.
Keep consultation with Varqa before delivering a Tablet.
Read the particular warning about delivering a letter between officials.
Preserve the explicit concern that circulating a letter could deepen hostility.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the Covenant! The letter that was written in defense against the calumniators of the people of Najaf-i-Ashraf - you must certainly keep it secure and give its copy to no one, for it will fall into the hands of the Yahyais and they will send it to Najaf, causing an increase in hatred and enmity.

order.why: Keep the account of temporarily removed ordinances and visible markers.
shortened: Furthermore, an exalted Tablet hath been revealed from the heaven of divine bounty, designated as the Most Holy Book.

Following the revelation of several verses concerning ordinances, which at this time it was not expedient to circulate, these were, by command, removed, and markers were placed at each location until such time as it may be fitting to restore them.

order.why: Retain the particular instruction concerning the tablets of arrival.
Read the instruction to copy and destroy specified papers as a source episode, not a general archival rule.
shortened: The papers you wrote are enclosed with this letter. Take a copy of them and be sure to destroy the original papers - their preservation is not permitted.

order.why: Keep the warning concerning unsealed papers within its covenantal controversy.
shortened: Any letter sent from this land without this servant's seal has the purpose of casting doubts, breaking the Covenant, demeaning the Center of the Cause of God, dividing the Word of God, and dispersing the gathering of the loved ones of God.

In any case, you must awaken the loved ones of the All-Merciful that they should never look at such unsealed papers, for their contents are purely misleading. Rather they should return them to this land so they may be given to their owner.

order.why: Read the harm of disturbing consciences and the sea-and-foam image.
Consider the critique of Gobineau through questions of access to witnesses.
shortened: As for the matter of the translation of Gobineau's book - the contents of that book do not conform to reality. For when Gobineau was in Iran, the Iranian government would immediately execute anyone suspected of being a Babi. No Babi dared utter a single word. Therefore what Gobineau heard were external accounts. He never inquired from any important figures. You have surely read it - it is clearly confused. In some places it is merely the imaginings of opponents with no truth whatsoever. The ignorant related such accounts and he wrote them down.

order.why: Read the concern about one-sided manuscript holdings in Paris.
shortened: O trustees of 'Abdu'l-Baha! Mr. Dreyfus has written from Paris and insisted with utmost emphasis that certain handwritten treatises from insignificant persons like the followers of Yahya are continuously arriving at the public library in Paris, and their purpose is to prevent the greatness of the Cause of God and the penetration of the Word of God and to promote their own vain imaginings. And since there are no handwritten treatises of this Cause in the public library, and since the scholars give more importance to handwritten treatises, they read these insignificant compositions.

order.why: Keep the proposal to send alternative reports through an intermediary.
Preserve the detailed polemical account of the disputed history as a claim of its source.
shortened: Now it has become evident--that is, the shameless followers of Yahya have prompted Browne to translate that book which they themselves, with consummate skill, had compiled and put together in the name of Aqa Mirza Jani as a history of the Cause, and had sent to the library in Paris.

From beginning to end, following the instructions and insinuations of the followers of Yahya, it has been written completely contrary to the facts, so that it might cause a distortion of minds and confusion of thoughts.

order.why: Keep the separate reported allegation of altered passages and publication.
Read the call for specific investigations and copies of a response.
Preserve the request for details from searched manuscript copies.
Bring multiple knowledgeable people together in the proposed response.
Keep the urgent instruction concerning Browne’s uncertainties in its setting.
Retain the brief judgment of a writing as spurious.
Read the request for information about Mirza Jani alongside care for Abu’l-Fadl.
shortened: O Abu'l-Fada'il! It is hoped from the favors of the Intended Lord that you are preserved and protected, for your existence and your writings are necessary for the service of the Cause of God, since you are entirely detached from self and the world and all therein.
Whatever information you have regarding the history of Mirza Jani the martyr, please write it down.

order.why: Preserve the particular arguments about rank and the contested history.
Keep the announcement of comprehensive responses to disputed books.
Retain the distinct concise rejection of the history’s attribution.
Read the prior review of a book and the response being prepared.
Keep the request for specified opposing books and the route of delivery.
Consider access to opponents’ writings as a condition for replying.
Read the acknowledgment that requested books arrived in time.
shortened: The books sent have arrived and came at a most opportune time. They were sent to Jinab-i-Abu'l-Fadl. This was a great service that will become a bridle for this sinner.

order.why: Keep the separate gratitude for obtaining previously unavailable books.
Preserve the notice of access through Hajji Niyaz.
Examine the qualified circulation of an external report despite acknowledged errors.
Keep the recourse to a further ruling in an unresolved case.
shortened: If accepted, well and good; if not, write confidentially to the Holy Land about the situation and a decisive ruling will come from there.

order.why: Preserve the question concerning proposed copying and the source’s stated lack of interest in those sciences.
Keep the specific school-related selection in its original context without generalizing its prohibition.
Read the warning against being veiled by a revealed text as a closing challenge.
shortened: The Exalted One saith: "Beware lest thou be veiled by that which hath been revealed in the Bayan."

order.why: Retain the account of a requested commentary, its delay and an existing civic treatise.
shortened: Among other things, in that Tablet nineteen planets were mentioned, and He stated that the full account had not yet been given. What was mentioned therein about the heavens and celestial spheres was different from what people commonly describe. In any case, He commanded the Most Great Branch - may my spirit and being be sacrificed for the most precious dust of His footsteps - to write a commentary on these matters.[AB00023] God willing, it will be sent later, but as He is currently occupied, it has been delayed. The treatise which was previously written concerning the civic governance[AB00004] is with Mulla 'Ali-Akbar - you will observe it.

order.why: Preserve the unrealized House of Translation proposal as a practical limitation.
Keep the original brief selection concerning a previously answered cemetery matter.
Retain the notice of requested writings already sent.
shortened: O dear friend of 'Abdu'l-Baha! Your letter which you had written to Aqa Siyyid Asadu'llah was noted. In it you had requested writings for certain blessed souls, but these had already been written and sent previously.

order.why: Keep the instruction concerning American apologetic materials.
Begin the later supplied statements with dignified and accurate presentation.
Read the 1971 statement’s scope and explicit description of review as temporary.
Consider the stated relation between broad teachings and institutional responsibilities.
Keep the warning against rigidity and the prospect of abolished restrictions.
Close with freedom of expression, conscience, and frank loving consultation held together.
shortened: Let us also remember that at the very root of the Cause lies the principle of the undoubted right of the individual to self-expression, his freedom to declare his conscience and set forth his views. If certain instructions of the Master are today particularly emphasized and scrupulously adhered to, let us be sure that they are but provisional measures designed to guard and protect the Cause in its present state of infancy and growth until the day when this tender and precious plant shall have sufficiently grown to be able to withstand the unwisdom of its friends and the attacks of its enemies. Let us also bear in mind that the keynote of the Cause of God is not dictatorial authority but humble fellowship, not arbitrary power, but the spirit of frank and loving consultation.

How do the examples of checking manuscripts, correcting translations, and comparing historical accounts help distinguish accuracy from mere agreement?

subjects.displayTitle: Two worlds, two books: reading creation and the life of the spirit
subjects.introduction: Going upstairs does not take you out of the house; the lower floor is still beneath you. With that homely picture ‘Abdu’l-Bahá settles a worry, the fear that to grow spiritually is to abandon the material. The body needs bread while the spirit feeds on meaning; the outward ear wants a melody while the inner ear waits for divine harmonies; material progress is praiseworthy so long as it does not close the eyes to the light shining in its midst. The world itself is one of two books, creation and revelation, written by the same Pen, and to read the camel, the heavens and the seas attentively is a form of devotion. Psalm 19 travels the same route, from the heavens telling the glory of God to the law that restores the soul and inward to the speaker’s hidden faults. Beyond this threshold lie health and healing, the two kinds of civilization a people can build, the difference between sight and insight, and the recognition that the higher and lower natures are two possibilities within one self.
subjects.arc: Enter through the house, wings, nourishment and two books; distinguish ways of knowing; explore embodied care and enduring value; follow the images into relationships, creativity and civilization; close with inward transformation and the unity of the self.

order.why: Unfold creation and revelation as two books.
shortened: The verse concerns this: there are two unfurled books - one the Book of Creation and the other the Book of Revelation. The Book of Revelation comprises the heavenly scriptures revealed unto the divine Prophets and issued from the pure mouth of Truth. The Book of Creation is this preserved tablet of contingent being and the unfurled scroll of existence, and Creation follows Revelation.

When thou readest Revelation, thou becomest aware of divine mysteries, and when thou gazest upon the Book of Creation, thou beholdest the signs, symbols, realities, conditions and manifestations of the hidden mystery and the outpourings of the Incomparable Lord.

order.why: Open with ascent within the same house.
Pair the two wings needed for flight.
shortened: Man has two powers; and his development, two aspects. One power is connected with the material world, and by it he is capable of material advancement. The other power is spiritual, and through its development his inner, potential nature is awakened. These powers are like two wings. Both must be developed, for flight is impossible with one wing.

order.why: Give body and spirit their proper nourishment.
Enlarge the book image to world and human fellowship.
shortened: For the Book there are meanings beyond counting, and likewise volumes beyond number. One volume thereof is the world itself, and the world itself is reckoned as a Book. It is that Book which encompasses all things and all regions of the world. One Book is inscribed by the Pen of Power and Creation, and one Book is written by the pen of the servants.

And one Book is [mentioned] in the Crimson Scroll, and it is specifically concerned with the mention of the gems of existence - they who regard the world as one country and who move amongst all with spirit and fragrance.

order.why: Bring the writing inward to tablets of hearts.
Pose correspondence between scientific inquiry and revelation.
Name outward appearance and inward reality.
Distinguish sensible and intelligible objects.
shortened: Know that created things are of two kinds: material and spiritual, sensible and intelligible. That is, some are perceptible to the senses while others are only perceived by the mind.

order.why: Test modes of understanding through visible and invisible examples.
shortened: There are two kinds of understandings: subjective and objective. To illustrate: thou seest this glass or this water and thou dost comprehend in a subjective manner their constituent parts. On the other hand thou cans't not see Love, Intellect, hate, Anger, Sorrow but thou dost recognize them in a subjective way through their signs and manifestations. The first is material, the second is spiritual. The first is outward, the second is intuitive. I hope that thou may'st make great advancement in the second kind of understanding.

order.why: Examine the distinction between bodily composition and intellect.
Read divine likeness as attributes rather than outward form.
Compare sight with insight and hearing with memory.
shortened: Man possesses two types of virtues: One is material, and the other ideal in character. For example, the body of man expresses certain material virtues, but the spirit of man manifests virtues that are ideal. The sense of sight in man is a physical virtue; but insight, the power of inner perception, is ideal in its nature. The sense of hearing is a physical endowment, whereas memory in man is ideal.

order.why: Use happiness as an intangible example.
Question the inference from unseen to nonexistent.
Preserve the reported critique of exclusive sense evidence.
Explore the limits imposed by a confined standpoint.
Clarify the language of Kingdom beyond spatial conditions.
Resist applying physical mixing to souls.
Retain the brief statement of different conditions.
Open the horizon of worlds beyond physical vision.
Invite thought beyond visible manifestations.
shortened: If such is what will take place in this visible world, then imagine what it will be in the spiritual realms of God, so exalted above the comprehension of all beings.

order.why: Scale the material universe through ray and ocean imagery.
Compare outward gifts with an unbounded inward horizon.
Hold expansiveness free of literal directions.
Locate spaciousness in heart and spirit.
Complicate a rigid inward-outward separation.
Retain the account connecting two worlds with dissension.
shortened: But beyond this, I want to use the opportunity presented to us by your question, in order to say something to you about the most profound cause of all dissensions:
Do not all the Prophets teach: there are two worlds, a spiritual one - the Malakut-i-Allah - the realm of God - and a material world, the world of nature in the widest meaning.

order.why: Place physical and spiritual needs within human life.
shortened: Herein we learn that man is a representative of the physical, intellectual and spiritual world. Just as in his physical environment he is in need of material things; in his spiritual environment he requires celestial things.
The physical world in comparison to the spiritual world is dark, for the physical world is ruled by the brute, blind forces of nature.

order.why: Return to the care required by both natures.
Join physical and spiritual perfections.
Keep the provinces of both forms of treatment.
shortened: Therefore, both of these have their provinces. Hence, both of them should be used -- both the one material and the other the spiritual. Neither of them has to be given up.

order.why: Make material care concrete through a bleeding cut.
shortened: Disease is of two kinds: (a) Material (b) Spiritual. For instance, a cut of the hand; if you pray for the cut to be healed, and do not stop it bleeding, you will not do much good, this needs a material remedy.
Sometimes if the nervous system is paralyzed through fear, a spiritual remedy is necessary.

order.why: Retain the reported conjunction of medicine and spiritual healing.
Affirm bodily health without equating disability with spiritual imperfection.
shortened: Nevertheless, both spiritual and physical health and well-being are desirable and commendable because they extend life. Thus, we should endeavor to acquire both a balanced spiritual life and physical health and progress. Both are desirable. But the foundation is the spiritual life. Once one possesseth this, though the body be afflicted with a disability, imperfection is not the result. But if the spiritual life is deficient, no matter how perfect one's physical life, it will yield no result. Nay, in the end it will be evident loss and the source of sorrow and despair during one's final days....

order.why: Give bodily health a role in effective service.
shortened: The importance lies not in the house but in its owner, who is unchanging and immutable. It is the spirit that delivers [man] from all physical worlds.

However, while the spirit is in the body, health must accompany it so that one may accomplish something. While the sun's rays are in this mirror, the mirror must be free from tarnish, pure and clear, but after the sun sets the mirror is useless.

order.why: Distinguish the weakened glass from the burning lamp.
shortened: Disease and illness are characteristics of the physical world, while health and well-being are among the subtle gifts of the divine realm. The body is like glass and the spirit like a lamp. If the glass becomes weakened, praise be to God the lamp is in its highest state of burning.

order.why: Separate bodily illness from inward health.
shortened: Though thou art physically sick and ill, praise be to God thou art spiritually sound and healthy, nay rather, enjoying perfect health.
Many of God's loved ones were afflicted with this ailment, but as they were blessed with true spiritual health, they paid no heed to it.

order.why: Attend to light as well as its vessel.
Retain the account of elemental bodily composition.
Contrast composition with the enduring spirit.
Turn the physician metaphor toward spiritual illness.
Follow a physician from bodily to inward care.
shortened: O accomplished physician! In the early part of your life you strove in physical medicine and discovered the causes and illnesses of this contingent body.

Now through the grace and generosity of the Intended One and through the abundant bounty of the Beloved Beauty, you have discovered the true divine medicine which is the life of spirits and health of hearts for people of success.

order.why: Differentiate remedies by the illness addressed.
Connect human spiritual capacity with divine bounty.
shortened: Man alone, by his spiritual power, has been able to free himself, to soar above the world of matter and to make it his servant.

Without the help of God man is even as the beasts that perish, but God has bestowed such wonderful power upon him that he might ever look upward, and receive, among other gifts, healing from His divine Bounty.

order.why: Set physical delicacy beside spiritual power.
Bring both kinds of education into the school.
shortened: And in the schools there must be both physical and spiritual training; for material sciences are as the body, and divine sciences as the spirit. The spirit must be breathed into the body, that the body may attain life. But if there be no spirit, the body is dead, though it be in the utmost beauty; since it is deprived of the bounty of the spirit, it beareth no fruit and yieldeth no result---nay, its nonexistence were better, for it becometh corrupt and fetid; assuredly it were better that it should be no more.

order.why: Place improvement of mind within human development.
shortened: The important factor in human improvement is the mind. In the world of the mind there must needs be development and improvement. There must be reformation in the kingdom of the human spirit; otherwise, no result will be attained from betterment of the mere physical structure.

order.why: Encourage heavenly arts and sciences.
Distinguish the intended reach of material and divine sciences.
Move from admired learning toward spiritual understanding.
Preserve the reported extension of scientific imagery toward spirit.
Introduce knowledge and meaning as distinct foods.
Ask what each food quickens.
Preserve the practical refusal to interfere with others’ material food.
Connect shared spiritual food with respect for customs.
shortened: We must each view with respect the customs of the other. There is a kind of food which needs neither knife nor fork and of which every one may partake with perfect ease and benefit. It is the food spiritual. This food brings life and stimulation instead of indolence and apathy. It brings peace and content to the one who partakes of it; the more food, the more joy and peace.

order.why: Let material hospitality mirror spiritual delight.
Compare the duration of two kinds of sustenance.
Name love and knowledge among spiritual foods.
Retain the invitation to the prepared table.
Question disproportionate attention to appetite.
Place comfort within the lover’s welcome.
Read a feast by its inward results.
shortened: The result of such a feast is the spirituality of the souls and the upliftment of the minds, while the outcome of the material feasts are temporal and superficial.

order.why: Ask for a gift that delights the heart.
Translate allowance into pearls of meaning.
shortened: Their allowance and stipend is from the mineral and vegetable kingdoms which fill the plains and wilderness. But your allowance and stipend consists of hidden pearls and protected gems that have been nurtured in the shell of grace in the depths of the sea of truth.

order.why: Retain the strong warning about refusing spiritual nourishment.
shortened: But as to those who deprive themselves of the Spiritual Table and of the Fragrance of the Spirit of God, they are dead and devoid of life. There is no immortality for them in this world nor in the kingdom of God.

order.why: Begin the inquiry into happiness with disappointed expectation.
shortened: Man erroneously thinks his happiness comes from the world and for that reason he is always unhappy and in difficulty.
For example, a man in poverty thinks if he were rich, he would be happy, but after attaining wealth he still finds himself unhappy and often in the very depths of sadness.

order.why: Examine the account of relief mistaken for lasting happiness.
shortened: As to material happiness, it never exists; nay, it is but imagination, an image reflected in mirrors, a specter and shadow. Consider the nature of material happiness. It is something. Which but slightly removes one's afflictions; yet the people imagine it to be joy, delight, exultation and blessing. All the material blessings, including food, drink etc. tend only to ally thirst, hunger and fatigue. They bestow no delight on the mind nor pleasure on the soul; nay, they furnish only the bodily wants. So this kind of happiness has no real existence.

order.why: Distinguish sensory pleasure from intellectual unfolding.
shortened: There are two kinds of happiness: Animal happiness and human happiness. Animal happiness is satisfied with the sight of green meadows, verdant woods, pure air and salubrious water. Such natural sights excites imagination, stirs the emotions and man becomes a dancing, laughing, care-free creature. But the unfoldment of human happiness depends upon the exercise of the hidden functions of intellect.

order.why: Allow lasting happiness to encompass material happiness.
Disentangle social rank from spiritual development.
Repeat that distinction through the image of sunlight.
shortened: A man may have attained to a high degree of material progress, but without the light of truth his soul is stunted and starved. Another man may have no material gifts, may be at the bottom of the social ladder, but, having received the warmth of the Sun of Truth his soul is great and his spiritual understanding is enlightened.

order.why: Preserve consolation amid material deprivation.
shortened: Though the earthly lamp in our nest and shelter is extinguished, we have a heavenly lamp. Though we are deprived of physical pleasures, we have an abundant share of spiritual sweetness and delight.

order.why: Place compassion within the test of wealth.
shortened: The hearts of the poor are sensitive; the hearts of the rich are hard. But if a rich man be compassionate, he is very near to God, for he has come out of temptation.

order.why: Locate spiritual wealth beyond poverty and riches.
Contrast finite treasure with sustaining inner wealth.
shortened: The search for earthly treasures befits the people of the earthly realm, not the sons and daughters of the Kingdom.
The earthly treasure comes to an end and causes physical life, but the treasure of the Kingdom is endless and causes spiritual life.

order.why: Retain the historical comparison with a wealthy man’s death.
Read encouragement after plunder in its addressed circumstances.
Compare earthly sovereignty with enduring grace.
Set mineral jewels beside spiritual adornment.
shortened: The adorning of the earthly crown is mineral gems and stones. The embellishment of this other crown are the spiritual jewels of the Kingdom of God. That earthly reign is the cause of pain and afflictions. But this other sovereignty is all happiness, joy and glad tidings.

order.why: Distinguish reputation from the reality it names.
Free true elevation from physical height.
Ask what survives physical conditions.
Retain the account of enduring reality and passing forms.
shortened: Only the spirit is real; everything else is as shadow. All bodies are disintegrated in the end; only reality subsists. All physical perfections come to an end; but the divine virtues are infinite.

order.why: Concentrate the distinction in one brief statement.
Compare physical likeness with merciful character.
Expand the horizon of virtue beyond material limits.
shortened: No matter how much the world of humanity advances in material civilization, it is nevertheless in need of the spiritual development mentioned in the Gospel. The virtues of the material world are limited, whereas divine virtues are unlimited.

order.why: Retain the warning about material forces gaining ascendancy.
Question attachment amid abundant gifts.
shortened: The All Glorious God has vouchsafed infinite bounty to the world of man and he has made man to be the descending place of heavenly grace. So in spite of all this bounty why does he attach his heart to this ephemeral world and close his eyes to the spiritual world?

order.why: Make motion without progress visible in the mill image.
shortened: They are like that donkey at the mill that toils around the millstone. It rotates around its pivot, unable to make any progress. From morning to evening that beast of burden does not progress by a single step though it is moving all the time, for its path is the track of the mill. Humankind too is in continuous motion, yet does not move away or upward from the centre of dust but simply circles around this contingent world instead.

order.why: Challenge the reduction of human purpose to material service.
Read the cage metaphor alongside earlier care for the body.
Echo the aspiration for release into a wider life.
shortened: They seek deliverance from the cage of this mortal realm and search for life in the expansive atmosphere of the heavenly Kingdom.

order.why: Define freedom through kindness and overcoming competitive struggle.
Compare natural struggle with the acquisition of perfections.
shortened: Just as in the natural world there is the struggle for existence, and this is the means of progress and growth and development of things, in the world of the spirit it is the acquisition of human perfections, and this law is the cause of the progress of spirits and the attainment of spiritual bounties.
The natural world in relation to that is a prison, preventing the comfort of thought and freedom of human conscience.

order.why: Contrast orientations of the soul.
shortened: O soul that yearneth for the Beloved! The worldly soul is closely bound to the world of dust and is far removed from the beauty of the celestial world. The divine soul is an intimate of the self-subsistent Lord and is privy to the world of mystery. The earthly soul returneth to the earth, whilst the divine soul returneth unto the Lord of lords.

order.why: Retain the strong contrast of birds and earthworms.
shortened: O ye sons and daughters of the Kingdom! Thankful, the birds of the spirit seek only to fly in the high heavens and to sing out their songs with wondrous art. But the pitiable earthworms love only to tunnel into the ground, and what a mighty struggle they make to get themselves down into its depths! Even so are the sons of earth.

order.why: Read differing responses through images of fragrance and light.
Preserve the account of response to revelation.
shortened: O daughter of the Kingdom! When the Sun of Truth dawned from the horizon of Iran, every soul that belonged to the world of nature - that is, whose element of existence was purely earthly - remained completely veiled and deprived. Every soul that belonged to the divine realm and whose existence partook of the element of the Kingdom turned towards it and beheld its lights.

order.why: Contrast limitation with reception of bounty.
Trace development toward light or darkness.
Move from passion’s rule toward divine government.
shortened: O thou who art longing for the Face of the All-Glorious!

In the realm of material existence, the sovereign of passion holds sway, and in the diseased clime of the carnal self, the evil king of pride wears the crown. But in the world of spirit, the Lord God is the Ruler.

order.why: Name the ethical difference as selfishness or mercy.
Bring spiritual orientation to everyday disturbance.
Consider the claimed reach of spiritual will.
Distinguish spiritual aspiration from physical phenomena.
shortened: What is needed is to rise above the material to the realms of the purely Spiritual. Table-turning and such like were material, a natural result, and not spiritual.

order.why: Introduce preparation through the womb analogy.
shortened: When man is in the world of the womb, God showers upon him all blessings. He gives him all the organs, eyes, ears, etc. But man cannot put this favour into use there; it is not manifest there. When the child is born from the world of the womb into this world, then all those blessings and gifts which God showered upon him in the world of the womb become manifest and useful.

order.why: Examine that analogy’s limits of present awareness.
shortened: The child in the womb may be imperfect -it may lack eyes, or ears, or limbs; yet it does not realise its blindness, its deafness, or its other imperfections. Neither its perfections nor its imperfections can be appreciated there. But when it comes to the world of men, its perfections and imperfections both become apparent.

order.why: Apply preparation to the soul’s present life.
shortened: This is the matrix world for the soul, even as the womb was the matrix world for the body or vehicle. - Birth into consciousness of another world begins here, a world for which this physical and material one is but the preparation and foundation."

order.why: Retain the image of birth into the Kingdom.
shortened: When a man is born into the world of phenomena he finds the universe; when he is born from this world to the world of the spirit, he finds the Kingdom.'

order.why: Preserve the answer concerning release from worldly limitations.
Read the strong contrast between worlds as reported.
shortened: This is a world of blindness, deafness, nothingness; the other world is a world of seeing, hearing, reality. This is a world of death, that of life. Man knows nothing in this world; the spiritual world is a world of revelation.

order.why: Keep existence open beyond the present horizon.
shortened: But praise be to God, the world of existence does not culminate here. If this were so, existence itself would be sterile. There are many worlds of light.

order.why: Compare temporal affliction with an enduring kingdom.
shortened: The material kingdom is of time; affliction and calamity attend it. It is the womb of pain. But the spiritual kingdom is unpassing, it has no end, it is beyond danger and fear, it is exalted day by day, its sun is shining ever more, the voice of its grandeur arises higher and higher. All that belongs to this visible world is corruptible, mortal; all that belongs to the divine world is incorruptible, eternal.

order.why: Retain the relative use of the term life.
shortened: Thus the life and existence of earthly persons compared to heavenly life and existence cannot be called life. If this physical life had any importance, Christ would not have accepted crucifixion.

order.why: Place relative life and death within the Adam and Eve explanation.
shortened: Likewise, material life, compared to eternal existence and the life of the Kingdom, is regarded as death. Thus Christ referred to this material life as death and said, "Let the dead bury their dead." Although those souls enjoyed material life, yet in His eyes that life was even as death.

order.why: Distinguish kinds of life through mirage and sea.
shortened: O Mirza Yuhanna! This name is derived from "life", but life is of two kinds: physical and spiritual. The first belongs to the realm of vain imaginings and is like the waves of a mirage, while the second is the outpouring of the clouds and is like a sweet and flowing sea. That one is a passing shadow, and this one a shining star.

order.why: Contrast earthly homelessness with a spiritual dwelling.
shortened: His Holiness, the Christ, the Holy Manifestations and the apostles possessed no nest whatsoever in this mortal world but in the universe of God, a glorious palace.

order.why: Offer the homeless reader an image of sanctuary.
shortened: Thou art a bird of the shelter of divine unity, and thy true nest is on the branches of the Tree beyond which there is no passing. Even though thou are utterly bereft of hearth and home in the path of God, thy true habitation is beneath His divine sanctuary.

order.why: Carry the crown image beyond physical departure.
shortened: The divine friends are the crowned rulers of the realm of inner meanings, and when they conceal their faces from the earthly kingdom, they shall adorn themselves with crown and diadem in the radiant world.

order.why: Acknowledge a gift not yet fully perceptible.
shortened: This is a great gift from God and hath no equal; although in this physical world its greatness is not perceivable, nor its nature clearly known, yet in the spiritual world it shineth like the sun.

order.why: Allow unseen radiance to have visible consequences.
shortened: And now that radiant star shines so bright and luminous that its rays extend from the unseen realm to the visible plane and become a bounty of existence. Soon you will observe even in this material world how brilliant and effulgent are the rays of that star.

order.why: Distinguish outward sight from enduring insight.
shortened: This outward eye shall turn to dust, but the inner vision shall remain eternal and steadfast in the pure world.

order.why: Place that distinction in an address to blind readers.
shortened: The sight of the physical and ordinary eye will some day pass away. Only for a short time does the eye exercise its function; then it becomes shut. But the power of insight is eternal; it is a heavenly gift, and through it man discovers the Kingdom. Through it he can see aright the beauty of God and the holy verities, and can discern the very mysteries of God.

order.why: Expose the limits of a spatial account of heaven.
Question literal readings that obscure spiritual meanings.
Preserve the account of Christ’s kingdom and reality.
Retain the reported contrast of Christ’s two bodies.
Keep the compact Christ-spirit comparison attributed.
shortened: The difference between Christ and others is this:  Christ was the Spirit, others are bodies.  Christ was the Sun, others are mirrors.  Christ was the Truth and was bestowing Eternal Life; others are dead and are imparting deadness and negligence.

order.why: Examine outward sacramental form and inward meaning.
Contrast expectations of a material and spiritual kingdom.
shortened: The people did not know of the spiritual kingdom of Jesus Christ, but they were waiting for a man to come who had a material kingdom.

order.why: Retain the historical polemic within its particular source.
Pair the second account of Paul’s heavenly flight.
Return from metaphysics to friendship across distance.
Locate nearness in affection.
Free spiritual relationship from geographical limits.
Preserve longing for both spiritual and bodily meeting.
Compare physical proximity with enduring union.
shortened: For nearness in the mortal realm is often followed by remoteness in the Kingdom, and physical union is pursued by spiritual separation. But this spiritual union's attribute is eternity and its characteristic is everlastingness.

order.why: Center connection in heart and reality.
Retain the affectionate language of spiritual kinship.
Apply parenthood to those formed in spirit.
Read scriptural family relationships spiritually.
Examine the claim of lasting spiritual love.
shortened: There are two kinds of Love - the material and the spiritual. Material love means the attachment of men to each other, whether it be friendship or any other relation and it always ends in grief, for the spiritual love is the only enduring love.

order.why: Retain the distinction between sex and spirit.
Use the swift spiritual letter to renew the distance image.
shortened: However, with a spiritual pen, at every moment he writes a divine letter, and this is accomplished with the utmost speed, for the physical world is a strange confinement - all its affairs are slow, and at most only a few steps can be taken in each breath. But the spirit traverses East and West in an instant. Consider how different these are!

order.why: Pair outer deprivation with inward hearing and sight.
shortened: Though the physical eye was prevented from beholding His enchanting countenance, the eye of the spirit is illumined by the lights of His divine Beauty. And though the outward ear was deprived of hearing His blessed words, the ear of the soul is delighting in the call to awareness from His most glorious Kingdom.

order.why: Distinguish bodily experience and inward vision.
shortened: O thou who art bound to the supernal world and the Concourse on high! Whatever is experienced by the outward body deriveth from this lower and inferior world, and whatever is perceived and witnessed by the eye of the soul and inward vision deriveth from the supernal world.

order.why: Join earthly embodiment with heavenly orientation.
shortened: Such souls though apparently earthy yet in reality they are heavenly; their body is of the phenomenal world and yet their spirit (emanated) from the world of God.

order.why: Preserve the explicit correction that spirit is in the flesh.
Let music and landscape show physical effects on spirit.
Explore the reported communion with the natural world.
Read trees through attention to their sustaining forces.
shortened: Another who looks at trees. He thinks of the effect and energy of the sun the effect of the breeze that blows; the influence and effect of rain' who has educated these trees. Viewpoints are different.

order.why: Hear the poetic image of nature’s communication.
shortened: It as though the trees, the rocks, the sea, the grass, the stars hold communion with man and whisper into his ears the secrets of nature.

order.why: Retain the account of things present before the divine throne.
shortened: And beyond this, at all times the realities of all things are present before the Divine Throne and recount what has befallen them, but people are unaware and do not comprehend.

order.why: Turn attention toward handiwork in the realm of meaning.
Compare arrangements that comfort senses and stir conscience.
Distinguish musical effects within the reported account.
Attend to meaning carried by song.
Preserve encouragement to a singer toward lasting success.
Bring remembrance into plowing, sowing and harvest.
Turn painting into a metaphor for deeds.
shortened: Man can paint those ideal pictures upon the Tablet of existence with the brush of deeds.

order.why: Join physical painting with images of spiritual qualities.
shortened: There are many physical painters who draw with utmost skill, but you are both a physical painter and a spiritual painter. You paint spiritual images with utmost skill and love, and those spiritual images are faith, assurance, and firmness in the Covenant and Testament.

order.why: Keep the corresponding reported account of two arts.
Question technical perfection without spiritual awareness.
shortened: 'Again,' He continued, 'look at the spider. What artist could create anything better made than a spider's web? Even so those artists whose creations are perfect, and who themselves are ignorant of the life of the spirit, are like the mole and the spider, far below the level of the man of faith.'

order.why: Move from external pictures to the heart’s mirror.
shortened: These things about here that you have pictured will all pass away, but the true picture is the one you take on the mirror of the heart.

order.why: Retain praise of writing devoted to spiritual life.
Read the extended newspaper metaphor as an image.
shortened: The thoughts of this newspaper is material but the conceptions of that newspaper are spiritual. The Editor of this newspaper is a man but the Editor of that newspaper is His Holiness Baha'u'llah. The subscribers to this newspaper are frail humanity but the subscribers to that newspaper are the angels of the supreme Concourse. The policies of this newspaper are earthly but the policies of that newspaper are heavenly. The pages of this newspaper are made of perishable materials but the pages of that newspaper are made with the celestial texture.

order.why: Preserve the historical physical explanation while distinguishing spiritual light.
Compare electric illumination with a celestial lamp.
shortened: O luminous lamp! The greatest of lamps, the electric light, nevertheless illumines only a limited distance nearby for several hours and miles. But the celestial lamp shines like the brilliant morning light unto the horizons, its light spreading from the earthly kingdom to the heavenly kingdom, and its radiance extending from the Supreme Concourse to the human realm.

order.why: Bring light into heart and soul.
Link physical and spiritual growth through two suns.
Use warmth to describe renewed love.
shortened: In the material world there is nothing but lethargy, rigidity and coldness, but the heat of the Sun of Truth rising from the horizon of the Kingdom will dispel this coldness and perfect the warmth of the love of God.

order.why: Read animating fire as the flame of heart and soul.
Apply the body-and-spirit image to existence.
shortened: The world of existence is like the human body - material forces are like its organs and parts. But this body needs a spirit to animate it, to give it life and vitality, to endow it with sight, hearing, memory and perception, so that the light of intellect may shine within it.

order.why: Distinguishes bodily life from the life of the spirit.
Use the crescent’s two faces to imagine completed capacities.
Affirm material progress while refusing spiritual neglect.
shortened: But, take heed, lest in thinking too earnestly of the things of the body you forget the things of the soul: for material advantages do not elevate the spirit of a man.

It is indeed a good and praiseworthy thing to progress materially, but in so doing, let us not neglect the more important spiritual progress, and close our eyes to the Divine light shining in our midst.
Only by improving spiritually as well as materially can we make any real progress, and become perfect beings.

order.why: Make material civilization support inward education.
Preserve the body-without-spirit warning.
shortened: Civilization is like unto the body. Spirituality is like the soul. A body without spirit is unprofitable, though it should be of the utmost beauty, while without spirit, it is as nothing.

order.why: Situate that warning in the reported view of Europe.
Keep the severe Paris metaphor in its historical source.
Follow with hope for both capacities in San Francisco.
shortened: San Francisco has capacity -- capacity for many things. It has both material and spiritual capacity, and is progressive. Just as this city is achieving material progress I am hopeful that it may also achieve ideal progress, and that through the divine illumination heavenly civilization may be established here.

order.why: Relate material association to spiritual fellowship.
shortened: Material civilization advances through the physical association of mankind. The progress you observe in the outer world is founded mainly upon the fraternity of material interests. Were it not for this physical and mental association, civilization would not have progressed. Now -- praise be to God! -- the indissoluble spiritual association is evident; therefore, it is certain that divine civilization has been founded, and the world will progress and advance spiritually.

order.why: Ask what roots material projects in lasting fruit.
Link spiritual support with livelihood and human welfare.
shortened: The other kind are those affairs which contribute toward the maintenance of livelihood, adding to the comfort, happiness and progress of the human family. Spiritual powers always come to the assistance of such affairs, they increase the moral insight and responsibility of man and add to his awareness and mindfulness."

order.why: Make justice and comfort an expression of spiritual capacity.
shortened: But humans, through their rational faculties and conscientious feelings, have been distinguished from other creatures so they may delve into spiritual matters, discover the realities of things, be attracted to the Supreme Kingdom, strive for human welfare and the comfort of humanity, and promote the means of justice and fairness.

order.why: Distinguish forms and reach of assistance.
shortened: Assistance is of two kinds:- Material assistance and spiritual assistance. Material assistance is limited to one locality and place but spiritual assistance is measureless.

order.why: Apply the physician image to a suffering society.
Retain the wartime image of predatory human relations.
Redirect military ingenuity toward interdependence.
Question the exhausted instrument of the sword.
shortened: The sword has been working over six thousand years and has become dull. We must look about us for another sword to take its place.

order.why: Compare conquests by their effects on human life.
Oppose conquest by love to humiliation by force.
shortened: But the conquests of the Baha'is are spiritual conquests, and these are a thousand times greater than outward conquests. For this conquest is through love, through knowledge, and pure grace, while that conquest is through arrows, through swords, through schemes and humiliation. This conquest bestows spirit and brings to life, while that conquest destroys foundations and casts souls into the pit of destruction. This conquest is eternal while that conquest is temporary, for in the Qur'an it states "Such days We alternate among the people."

order.why: State spiritual victory’s human purpose.
shortened: Victory is of two kinds: material and spiritual. Material victory is not so important but spiritual victory is conducive to the life of the world of humanity.

order.why: Consider the endurance ascribed to prophetic conquests.
Turn the struggle inward through the jihad tradition.
shortened: For this reason the following tradition is recorded from the lips of a god-fearing adept: 'From minor Jihad we have turned our attention to the major Jihad;- that is, we have quitted fighting with the outside enemy and are concentrating our forces on the defeat of the inside foe - the foe of the spirit. This is interpreted as the real Jihad.
