order.why: Read spiritual resistance within the East-West warning.
Keep the related historical claim attributed.
Preserve the figurative victory of oppressed believers.
shortened: However, the oppressed ones of the All-Merciful, through divine power, brought the face of the earth into the curve of their polo stick and occupied themselves with heaven.

order.why: Distinguish sources of worldly and spiritual authority.
shortened: The physical or natural leader of the people is selected by the people, but the Heavenly Leader is selected by the Lord.  A material leader, if a king, is mighty by the sword, and if a president, is powerful by the consensus of opinion.  The Heavenly Ruler is mighty through Divine Bounty, and the election of the Holy Spirit, and through the Power of the Love of God.

order.why: Compare earthly leadership with spiritual responsibility.
shortened: Say: O chief of tribes! Although this station among the tribes and clans is lofty and honored, yet the chieftainship of heavenly tribes and the leadership of spiritual clans has another station and a different glory.

order.why: Locate power in hearts rather than possession.
Concentrate the concern on heart and soul.
shortened: Our work concerns the heart and soul, not water and clay.

order.why: Retain the breadth of spiritual activity amid hardship.
shortened: And despite a hundred thousand hardships and the onslaught of all tribes - Arab, Turk and Tajik - this is the expansive realm of the Kingdom of the Creator-King, and the vast arena of the world of spirit and dominion, with its bounties, bestowals and insight.

order.why: Distinguish physical destruction from loss of teachings.
shortened: His intention is destruction, and it is divided into two parts, one physical and the other spiritual. The physical abomination of desolation is the razing and destroying of buildings. The spiritual abomination of desolation is the destruction of the teachings of GOD.

order.why: Imagine a collective center of merciful feeling.
Associate spiritual power with peace and love.
Direct attention to elevating human life.
shortened: In other words, they must promote the principles of the sublimity of the human world, which is loftier than this fictitious heaven, and spread the light of the Luminary of the Merciful Universe, which is more radiant and luminous than the stars studded in yon blue dome.

order.why: Close the social movement with a transformed garden.
Echo the hope for an illumined earth.
Bring that hope into encouragement to one person.
Gather the senses into a vision of spiritual development.
Ask how one can live on earth with heavenly orientation.
shortened: Endeavor as much as possible to liberate thyself wholly from human susceptibilities-so that the powers of the Kingdom may gain control over thy heart and thy spirit-to such a degree that although thou art living on the face of the earth, yet thou mayest truly be in heaven; that although outwardly thou an composed of material elements, yet spiritually thou mayest become composed of heavenly elements.

order.why: Focus aspiration through service.
shortened: If thou wouldst hearken to the divine counsel detach thyself from all such thoughts and sanctify thyself utterly from all these contaminations. Seek for the servitude of the Abha Beauty alone so that thou mayest be a prince amongst princes and a ruler in the world above.

order.why: Let truth dispel prejudice.
shortened: Pay not attention to things material but reach after the Spirit. Fix your eyes on the Sun of Truth for his light floods the whole earth. Let the sun give you of his strength then the clouds of prejudice will not hide his light from your eyes, then will the sun be without clouds for you.

order.why: Turn the desired transformation into prayer.
Return to the prayer’s two kingdoms.
shortened: Then let him stand up, and facing the Qiblih (Point of Adoration, i.e., Bahji, 'Akka), let him say:
God testifieth that there is none other God but Him. His are the kingdoms of Revelation and of creation.

order.why: Recall the covenant across revelation and creation.
shortened: Thou didst establish His covenant with every one who hath been created in the kingdoms of earth and heaven and in the realms of revelation and of creation.

order.why: End the linked readings with praise across both realms.
shortened: Unto Him pertaineth all glory and majesty in the kingdoms of Revelation and Creation and whatever lieth between them.

order.why: Close with the supplied clarification that two tendencies do not mean two separate selves.

questions: How does going upstairs within the same house illuminate the relation between material life and spiritual growth? Where might that image reach its limits?
What changes when creation and revelation are approached as two books, and what habits of attention does each kind of reading require?
How do the passages on food, healing, education, and art qualify the strong contrasts between body and spirit elsewhere in the compilation?
Which forms of success or happiness seem enduring here, and how might their pursuit change relationships, work, and the use of wealth?
How does Psalm 19’s movement from the heavens to divine instruction and self-examination compare with the movement between the two books in these readings?
What becomes clearer when the higher and lower tendencies are understood as possibilities within one self, and which connected subject would help you explore that further?

references.label: 1 · Psalm 19 · Creation, instruction, and inward examination
references.note: Follow the psalm from the heavens and the sun to divine instruction, then to the speaker’s hidden faults and inward meditation. Compare this movement with the two books of creation and revelation. The psalm offers praise and prayer rather than a theory of two worlds; how does its changing focus alter the reader’s responsibilities?

subjects.displayTitle: Justice: from a searching eye to a society of mutual protection
subjects.introduction: Everyone speaks of fairness, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes, and if words were enough humanity would long since have prospered. Justice begins instead with something as plain as a workman paid his wage at the end of the day, a servant beaten by a Pasha who then discovers that the law reaches him too, and a majority in need while a few live in luxury. Bahá’u’lláh calls justice the light of men and says its purpose is unity: to see with one’s own eyes rather than through imitation, and, as ‘Abdu’l-Bahá adds, to regard humanity as a single body in which an injury to any member is felt by all. Rulers are asked to weigh themselves daily in the balance of equity before judging anyone else; communities, to protect minorities and the poor; each person, neither to defraud a neighbour nor to yield to being defrauded. The Qur’an’s demand for truthful witness even against oneself or one’s kin brings the same impartiality home. The path leads on into fair-mindedness and the pairing of justice with mercy, into labour, profit sharing and the moderation of wealth, into race unity, and into the twin pillars of reward and punishment, until a world that praises justice becomes one that practises it.
subjects.arc: Begin with the distance between proclaimed justice and lived conditions; develop fair perception and equal rights; examine protection, governance and economic arrangements; distinguish mercy, accountability and divine judgment; return through lament and hope to concrete communal responsibility.

order.why: Make the choice personal for worker as well as ruler.
Open by testing words against actual prosperity.
Bring inequality into the question of what justice means.
Give justice a concrete form in the worker’s wage.
shortened: Know that justice consists in rendering to each his due. For example, when a workman labours from morning till evening, justice requires that he be paid his wage, but bounty consists in rewarding him even when he has done no work and expended no effort.

order.why: Name human unity as its purpose.
shortened: The word of God which the Supreme Pen hath recorded on the sixth leaf of the Most Exalted Paradise is the following: The light of men is Justice. Quench it not with the contrary winds of oppression and tyranny. The purpose of justice is the appearance of unity among men. The ocean of divine wisdom surgeth within this exalted word, while the books of the world cannot contain its inner significance.

order.why: Connect justice with independent, searching perception.
Expand impartiality through humanity as one body.
shortened: The second attribute of perfection is justice and impartiality. This means to have no regard for one's own personal benefits and selfish advantages, and to carry out the laws of God without the slightest concern for anything else. It means to see one's self as only one of the servants of God, the All-Possessing, and except for aspiring to spiritual distinction, never attempting to be singled out from the others. It means to consider the welfare of the community as one's own. It means, in brief, to regard humanity as a single individual, and one's own self as a member of that corporeal form, and to know of a certainty that if pain or injury afflicts any member of that body, it must inevitably result in suffering for all the rest.

order.why: Begin practice with guarded speech and fair judgment.
shortened: Be fair in thy judgment, and guarded in thy speech.
Be unjust to no man, and show all meekness to all men.

order.why: Require implementation beyond terminology and meaning.
Join refusal to defraud with refusal to accept fraud.
Distinguish generosity from yielding to wrongful taking.
Value justice beyond nationality and familiarity.
Extend recognition across nations and governments.
shortened: The Baha'is are free from all prejudices, are well-wishers of the human world, are lovers of justice and good governance, and praise these qualities from whichever government or nation they may emerge.

order.why: Establish an equal standard of human rights.
Place all under the same protection.
Preserve the parallel declaration of equal standing.
Link equality with divine kindness.
shortened: God is just and kind to all. He considers all as His servants. He excludes none, and His judgments are correct and true.

order.why: State rights through ordinary human needs.
Join rights with spiritual solidarity.
Retain the addressed statement of equality among relatives.
Move from one nation toward protection of all nations.
shortened: I counsel them that they may day by day strengthen the bond of love and amity to this end---that they may become the sympathetic embodiment of one nation---that they may extend themselves to a universal Brotherhood to guard and protect the interest and rights of all the nations of the East---that they may unfurl the Divine Banner of justice---that they may realize and treat each nation as a family composed of the individual children of God and may know that before the sight of God the rights of all are equal.

order.why: Connect the overcoming of prejudice with universal mercy.
Situate rights and freedom within relationships.
shortened: And among the teachings of Baha'u'llah are justice and right. Until these are realized on the plane of existence, all things shall be in disorder and remain imperfect. The world of mankind is a world of oppression and cruelty, and a realm of aggression and error.

Similarly, with regard to the peoples who clamour for freedom: the moderate freedom which guarantees the welfare of the world of mankind and maintains and preserves the universal relationships, is found in its fullest power and extension in the teachings of Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Hold equity together with kindness to every soul.
Make kindness and justice sources of strength.
shortened: A child cannot kill a man; but a Bonaparte can abstain from war, from shedding blood, from devastating countries. A dumb person will not speak ill of any one, a paralyzed hand cannot strike; but a strong arm can refrain from striking. Justice, love and kindness must be the instruments of strength, not of weakness.

order.why: Find power in humility rather than dominance.
shortened: O My handmaiden! Lowliness is the cause of elevation and justice is the source of power. Consider the lowliness of dust - from it pure jewels appear, and from the earth the Manifestations of the names of the Lord of Lords become manifest and evident.

order.why: Pair fairness and justice as enabling wings.
shortened: Justice and fairness are as two wings for the servants of God, and blessed is the state of the soul that hath attained unto these twain and become detached from all that is in the world and in the realm of creation.

order.why: Apply justice to the corrosions of daily relationships.
Unite justice, kindness and human dignity.
shortened: They are ever observant of justice and fairness.
They should hold fast to justice, kindness and fairness so that all may attest to that which bespeaks the loftiness of human station.

order.why: Retain the account of care for emigrants and kin.
Read an addressed dispute through law and generous character.
Keep the particular testimony ruling in its historical setting.
shortened: The testimony of his brothers, his sisters, and his wife is testimony affirming the fact; while the testimony of the former wife and her helper is testimony denying it. In all the laws of the world, affirmative testimony taketh precedence over negative testimony. His brothers and his wife bear witness affirming that he was a Baha'i, while others deny it; and witnesses who affirm are preferred over witnesses who deny. Their testimony is accepted; the testimony of the others is rejected.

order.why: Preserve the application of justice to marriage in its source.
Ask for reciprocity between the parties.
Place voluntary preference for others beside reason and equality.
Retain the broader account of self-forgetting service.
Move from personal practice to binding the broken and restraining oppression.
Give rulers responsibility for the weak person’s rights.
Define the royal diadem as aid to the oppressed.
Place the ruler’s self-examination before judgment of others.
shortened: The Great Being saith:  The heaven of statesmanship is made luminous and resplendent by the brightness of the light of these blessed words which hath dawned from the dayspring of the Will of God:  It behoveth every ruler to weigh his own being every day in the balance of equity and justice and then to judge between men and counsel them to do that which would direct their steps unto the path of wisdom and understanding.  This is the cornerstone of statesmanship and the essence thereof.

order.why: Repeat that examination as a daily discipline.
shortened: Set before thine eyes God's unerring Balance and, as one standing in His Presence, weigh in that Balance thine actions every day, every moment of thy life. Bring thyself to account ere thou art summoned to a reckoning, on the Day when no man shall have strength to stand for fear of God, the Day when the hearts of the heedless ones shall be made to tremble.

order.why: Ask government to know conditions and appoint by merit.
shortened: Governments should fully acquaint themselves with the conditions of those they govern, and confer upon them positions according to desert and merit. It is enjoined upon every ruler and sovereign to consider this matter with the utmost care that the traitor may not usurp the position of the faithful, nor the despoiler rule in the place of the trustworthy.
O people of God! That which traineth the world is Justice, for it is upheld by two pillars, reward and punishment. These two pillars are the sources of life to the world.

order.why: Connect intelligence, justice and public order.
Keep wisdom beside the exercise of justice.
shortened: Say: O people! Hold fast unto wisdom in all matters, for it profiteth you in all conditions, and I am the All-Knowing. It is the lamp of God among you and the light of justice for you, were ye of those who remember.

order.why: Contrast justice’s strength with conventional armies.
Explore justice as protection, order and love.
shortened: No light can compare with the light of justice. The establishment  of order in the world and the tranquillity of the nations depend upon it.

Justice is a powerful force. It is, above all else, the conqueror of the citadels of the hearts and souls of men, and the revealer of the secrets of the world of being, and the standard-bearer of love and bounty.

order.why: Use the lamp image to describe guidance amid danger.
Measure sovereignty by reform and prosperity.
Replace the jeweled crown with justice.
Retain the parallel crown account in its particular context.
shortened: They have written that they wish to sell some of the stones from Iran's crown. The crown of Iran is justice, not stones. If they can place a crown of justice upon this nation's head, that is proper. What benefit is there in a crown of stones? It is just stone. The ancient kings of Iran took pride in justice, not in a crown of stone.

order.why: Let a dying ruler’s regret question worldly power.
shortened: A king at the time of his death wished he was of the poor class. 'I wish I was poor!' he exclaimed. 'In the first place, I would not have ruled with injustice, and, in the second place, at the last moment, I would not be in such a state of remorse and regret!'

order.why: Examine the reported refusal of bribery and equal accountability.
shortened: "A certain Pasha, having most unjustly and cruelly beaten one of his servants, was arrested and brought before that just man who represented Britain. To the intense surprise of the Pasha, he himself was sentenced to a term of imprisonment, and told that he richly deserved the punishment. He could not think it possible that so great a person as himself could be sent to prison, and offered a large bribe for his release. This was sternly refused. A much larger sum was offered with the same result, and the unjust lord was compelled to accept the punishment awarded him for his cruelty to his servant.
"The news of this incident, being noised abroad, did much to show the Eastern people that British justice is in reality the same for the rich and for the poor, and therefore worthy of all respect."

order.why: Preserve praise of an effort toward equality in its historical setting.
shortened: In the 'Hidden Words' Baha'u'llah says 'Justice is to be loved above all.' Praise be to God, in this country the standard of justice has been raised; a great effort is being made to give all souls an equal and a true place.

order.why: Retain the account of security shared by believers and strangers.
shortened: Believers and unbelievers were at rest, and acquaintances and strangers were playing cheerful melodies. Verily, the darkness of injury ad error was uncovered by the light of equity and justice, and the government put on the garment of probity.

order.why: Keep praise of a regional ruler tied to its source.
Preserve the report of satisfaction with a leader’s conduct.
shortened: A group of friends offer endless praise for the excellent conduct, excellent policy and justice of His Excellency the Chosen One, and express complete satisfaction.

order.why: Retain the addressed praise of resistance to oppression.
shortened: The radiant sun of his equity rises high, and he is the humiliator and vanquisher of the people of oppression.

order.why: Connect a ruler’s justice with public tranquility.
Keep the personified banners in their addressed testimony.
Relate service to government with securing rights.
shortened: We beseech God that you may be assisted and confirmed at all times and under all conditions to serve that great monarch and to secure the rights of nations and justice and equity among peoples, and to render outstanding services to the eternal throne of sovereignty.

order.why: Preserve gratitude for a prisoner’s release and its stated response.
Retain the prayer for a sovereign to act justly.
Make protection of poor and weak the object of prayer.
Gather helpers of the distressed into an appeal for support.
Connect just government with public cooperation.
Keep the reported conjunction of capable government and active people.
Read the intervention claim within its historical argument.
Retain the specific remark about Russia with source context.
Preserve the encouragement toward freedom.
shortened: Do not yield to the overwhelming power of tyranny and despotism. Serve the cause of democracy and freedom. Continue your journey to the end.

order.why: Read a concrete appeal for protection after persecution.
shortened: In any case, now the government must, in gratitude for this divine confirmation, pursue justice and fairness and seek retribution for the martyred eminent scholar Aqa Siyyid Yahya in Sirjan, for that noble soul was, a few months ago, cut to pieces with utmost cruelty and hostility by the oppressors. Likewise, the government must offer complete protection to the oppressed ones of the world so that this divine confirmation and success may continue.

order.why: Retain petitioning counsel within the circumstances of oppression.
Preserve the appeal concerning those killed unjustly.
shortened: The enemies are delighted that ownerless property hath fallen to them. Have they not heard the decisive, mighty proclamation which saith: "For him who is slain unjustly, We have given authority to his heir."

order.why: Ask that what befits the oppressed party become clear.
shortened: We hope that through the all-encompassing hidden bounties, the lights of justice and fairness will shine forth and what befits the oppressed party will become manifest and determined.

order.why: Connect success with seeking justice.
shortened: Divine confirmation and success come through justice and the seeking of justice. And God is the protector of the oppressed.

order.why: Retain the hope that aggression will be restrained.
Preserve the invitation to help prevent harmful acts.
shortened: I hope that you will some day be able to hinder such actions, and thus enable justice to reign everywhere.

order.why: Protect peaceful people from attack.
Extend legal protection to animals.
Broaden settlement of disputes to an international tribunal.
shortened: Ultimately, war will be entirely banned, and when the laws of the Most Holy Book are enacted, arguments and disputes will, with perfect justice, be settled before a universal tribunal of governments and peoples, and any difficulties which may arise will be resolved.

order.why: Imagine one homeland under justice.
Trace the proposed social effects of just and merciful dealings.
Return to the servant’s pain beside the master’s comfort.
Make workers’ toil a reason for sharing profits.
Retain the associated proposal about shared gains.
Ask who benefits from labor-saving machines.
shortened: You cannot understand now, how the labor saving machines can produce leisure for mankind because at present they are all in the hands of the financiers and are used only to increase profits, but that will not continue. The workers will come into their due benefit from the machine that is the divine intention, and one cannot continue to violate the law of God.

order.why: Carry the historical slavery comparison into industrial conditions.
Introduce land, discovery and public benefit in the reported proposal.
Consider laws addressing extremes of wealth and poverty.
Place changed hearts alongside new economic laws.
Explore sacrifice on both sides of labor relations.
Preserve the question and answer about social and labor movements.
Keep the warning against injustice toward the rich.
shortened: The ruling power or government cannot treat the rich unjustly. To force them to divide their wealth would be unjust.

order.why: Examine the rejection of force even for a just claim.
Set cooperation against struggle for land.
Retain the vision of comfort without uniform social positions.
Question self-interest under a just social order.
shortened: Therefore we must all live in the utmost of happiness and comfort under a just rule and regulation in accordance with the laws of God, because this life is fleeting, and if man looks after himself only, he is no better than the animal, for the animal alone is to that degree egotistic.

order.why: Make comfort and welfare a universal aspiration.
Keep individual love and social justice in the same horizon.
Name abandonment of selfish interest as part of change.
shortened: Perchance, God willing, they may become mindful and aware, be released from negligence, abandon tyranny and oppression, treat each other with justice and fairness, and give up the dictates of selfishness and personal interest.

order.why: Retain the account of faith sustaining refusal to wrong another.
Distinguish public justice from forgiveness.
Locate social protection in institutions of justice.
Specify rights and property as objects of protective law.
Keep the reported strong statement about crime and punishment for comparison.
shortened: If a person commit a crime against you, you have not the right to forgive him; but the law must punish him in order to prevent a repetition of that same crime by others, as the pain of the individual is unimportant beside the general welfare of the people.

order.why: Connect retribution with security in its addressed case.
shortened: Justice requireth that judgment be passed upon him, and equity demandeth retribution for his deeds, that security and peace may be established.

order.why: Retain reward and punishment as pillars of public order.
Link accountability with human choice.
Preserve the claim that deeds have recompense.
shortened: In any case, every deed has its recompense, and every evil act has its consequent blow - divine justice demands this.

order.why: Keep the specific warning concerning slander.
shortened: However, the Lord of the Kingdom afflicts every audacious slanderer with abundant punishment. This is required by divine justice.

order.why: Retain the Báb’s prescribed restraint and compensation in its own legal setting.
Preserve the reported relation between individual and communal law.
Distinguish what is due from gratuitous bestowal.
Open the contrasting horizon of grace.
shortened: Regarding one's lack of capacity and one's undeserving on the Day of Resurrection, this does not cause one to be shut out from gifts and bounties; for this is not the Day of Justice but the Day of Grace, while justice is allotting to each whatever is his due.

order.why: Read due measure within the ordering of creation.
shortened: This is the station of justice, that is, giving to each one his due, and this is the station of the ordering of creation after its coming into being, and the degrees of destiny in creation and origination, even as was revealed from the Kingdom of eternity unto the Seal of the Prophets, peace and blessings be upon him: "And there is not a thing but with Us are the treasuries thereof, and We send it not down save in appointed measure."

order.why: Pair divine non-injury with human responsibility.
Acknowledge the limits of present understanding of divine justice.
shortened: Were the mysteries, that are known to none except God, to be unraveled, the whole of mankind would witness the evidences of perfect and consummate justice. With a certitude that none can question, all men would cleave to His commandments, and would scrupulously observe them.

order.why: Retain the paradox of justice seen in different outward conditions.
Examine revelation as the asserted source and balance of justice.
shortened: Know ye that the root of justice and its source is that which the Manifestation of God Himself ordaineth in His Day, were ye of them that know. Say: He is the Balance of Justice between the heavens and the earth, and though He should come with a cause that would strike terror into all in the heavens and on earth, verily this would be manifest justice.
Await ye, O people, the days of justice which have indeed come in truth. Beware lest ye be veiled from them and be of the heedless ones.

order.why: Keep the claim of divine judgment and human benefit.
shortened: We judge between people as We please and summon them unto that which shall profit them in the world to come and in this world.

order.why: Let the speaking Balance introduce accountability for deeds.
Explore its distinctions of truth and trustworthiness.
Retain the Báb’s invitation to fair judgment.
Keep the announced Day of Justice with its source omission visible.
shortened: O Muhit! Deliver thy Lord's decree with justice, for victory is ordained this day for the believers in that which is written...
We have promised mankind the Day of Justice and We have made clear the Cause that those in whose hearts is doubt concerning God's Command may come forth.

order.why: Preserve praise of Muhammad and the diffusion of equity.
Join the voice of justice with the opening of grace.
Retain the extended addressed testimony to revelation.
shortened: We testify that thou hast set thy face towards God and traveled far until thou didst attain His presence and gavest ear unto the Voice of this Wronged One, Who hath been cast into prison through the misdeeds of those who have disbelieved in the signs and testimonies of God and have denied this heavenly grace through which the whole world hath been made to shine. Blessed thy face, for it hath turned unto Him, and thine ear, for it hath heard His Voice, and thy tongue, for it hath celebrated the praise of God, the Lord of lords. We pray God to graciously aid thee to become a standard for the promotion of His Cause and to enable thee to draw nigh unto Him at all times and under all conditions.

order.why: Contrast manifested justice with human inattention.
Echo that failure to perceive.
Ask what obstructs the light of justice.
Connect justice with release from idle imagination.
shortened: When the standard of justice is raised, the hosts of fancy and idle imagination will flee. Blessed are they who know.

order.why: Preserve the exhortation to fair response in its figurative language.
shortened: Say: We have abandoned the carrion, inasmuch as the heavenly table hath been sent down from the heaven of the bounty of our Lord, the Mighty, the All-Praised. Fear ye God, O concourse of the ignorant ones! Deal fairly in that which hath appeared with truth, and be not of the lost.

order.why: Ask oppressed hearers to listen and reflect fairly.
Connect illumination with fair examination of revelation.
shortened: We beseech God not to deprive His servants of the splendors of the Sun of Justice, that all may consider with fairness that which hath appeared and been revealed.

order.why: Locate justice within the enumerated teachings.
shortened: And His teachings are these: First, the independent investigation of truth and deliverance from ancient traditions.
Twelfth, the Most Great Justice.

order.why: Make attainment of justice the desired end.
shortened: Whoso attaineth unto justice hath attained unto that which God, the Lord of all beings, hath desired.

order.why: Turn to the unsettling image of justice existing only in name.
shortened: Justice, like the phoenix, existeth in name but not in reality. Equity, like the philosopher's stone, is rare indeed.

order.why: Preserve the parallel phoenix and refuge image.
shortened: Justice, like the phoenix, naught remaineth of it save its name, and equity hath taken flight to the pavilions of glory, seeking refuge from the talons of the birds of darkness.

order.why: Hear the lament of equity under oppression.
shortened: Today the cry of justice is raised high and the lamentation of equity is uplifted. The darkness of oppression hath enveloped the world and its peoples.

order.why: Laments oppression through the personification of justice and equity.
Retain the denunciation of vanished justice.
shortened: Evil is that which they have wrought, and they shall have no portion of this Great Sea.
Discrimination hath vanished and justice hath perished.

order.why: Identify desire as a cloud over justice.
Ask about readiness to receive the obscured light.
Read tyranny through smoke and fire.
Retain the lament for wrong after the balance was established.
shortened: Perdition unto the people who wronged Thee after the balance of justice was established through Thee in the days of Thy Lord, the Most Glorious.

order.why: Preserve the warning of consequences for oppressors.
shortened: The oppressors shall soon behold the recompense of their deeds from the presence of a just and mighty Lord.

order.why: Keep the severe promise of punishment within its source.
shortened: Be not distressed by the tyranny of oppressors. God lies in wait - soon will He cast them all into the flames.

order.why: Contrast transient wrongdoing with divine sovereignty.
shortened: However, in the eyes of those endowed with vision who gaze toward the Most Great Horizon, those souls who turned away from the Truth and who wander in the wilderness of fancy and ignorance were and shall ever be the true prisoners. Soon shall the wrongdoer return to the lowest depths, and sovereignty shall remain with God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Retain the judgment against choosing tyranny.
Preserve the warning of an awakening from heedlessness.
Read the Pharaoh narrative as an example of recompense.
shortened: Thus were Pharaoh and his hosts drowned as recompense for their deeds. Verily God seized him for his sin and delivered Moses and his companions.

order.why: Place that narrative beside justice emerging from oppression.
shortened: Know thou with clear certainty that these great oppressions prepare the way for supreme justice. The tyranny of Pharaoh prepared the way for the justice of Moses, and the hand of power brought forth from his house that which he strove with all his might to avoid and whose removal he sought.

order.why: Retain the paradox of glory disclosed through suffered shame.
shortened: The shame I was made to bear hath uncovered the glory with which the whole of creation had been invested, and through the cruelties I have endured, the Daystar of Justice hath manifested itself, and shed its splendor upon men.

order.why: Read consolation and hoped-for justice in a letter about tribulations.
shortened: And concerning the tribulations that were mentioned, though outwardly they caused grief and sorrow, yet as they were borne for the sake of God, they were and shall ever be light upon light. The world is transient, as is evident in its constant change and transformation, and this very change is a tablet whereon its evanescence hath been inscribed by the Pen of Power. O blessed are they who possess insight! Ere long shall the carpet of tyranny be rolled up as it was before, and the carpet bearing the fruits of the deeds of the sincere ones shall be spread forth.

order.why: Recognize those not frightened away by tyranny.
shortened: The glory be upon thee and upon those whom tyranny hath not frightened nor prevented from turning unto the Countenance of Justice, through whose light the morn hath breathed and the Sun of Knowledge hath shone forth from the horizon of the providence of God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Return responsibility to deeds that obstruct justice.
shortened: Today is the day of utterance and exposition, and the day of unity and harmony. Had the loved ones held fast to the counsels recorded in the Tablets, they would now behold the world adorned and illumined with the light of justice and fairness. Some deeds act as barriers and veils. We beseech God to assist all to return and repent, and to arise to make good what hath escaped them.

order.why: Retain the repeated summons to fairness in Iran.
Extend the charge to all people.
shortened: We enjoined upon all men to be just and fair-minded and to fear God, the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Apply it within relations among believers.
Join pure justice with righteousness.
shortened: Say: Hold fast unto pure justice and unto that which ye have been commanded in the Book. He hath enjoined upon you righteousness and piety - to this His Most Exalted Pen beareth witness, and behind it the Revealer of verses.

order.why: Retain the command joining justice and piety.
Keep fair-mindedness within limits of just conduct.
shortened: And the glory be upon thee and upon all who are fair-minded and transgress not the decree of justice in God's Cause and are among the God-fearing.

order.why: Retain the addressed call to manifest justice among parties.
shortened: And We make mention of him who is named Muhammad Ja'far, and We counsel him and My loved ones to observe justice and fairness and that whereby the glory of My party shall be made manifest amidst all parties.

order.why: Preserve personal counsel to Asad.
shortened: O Asad! We have heard thy mention and have mentioned thee, and We counsel thee to observe justice and fairness and that which thou hast been commanded in the Book of God, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Preserve personal counsel joined with remembrance.
Condense the stated demand to fairness.
Repeat the universal social obligation.
shortened: Be just among men, for thus have ye been commanded in all the Tablets, did ye but know.

order.why: Connect the obligation with prescribed action.
shortened: He hath commanded all to observe justice and fairness, and to practice that which is prescribed in His perspicuous Book.

order.why: Pair the command with the prohibition of tyranny.
shortened: Verily We have commanded all to observe pure justice and forbidden them from tyranny in numerous Tablets.

order.why: Place the command in continuity with earlier counsel.
shortened: O ye who are the beloved of the All-Merciful throughout all possibilities! Hearken unto that which God commandeth you in the Book, and follow not the way of the mischief-makers. He commandeth you to observe justice, even as He commanded you aforetime. He, verily, is the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

order.why: Retain the concise invitation to hold fast.
shortened: Take hold of justice and fairness by Our command, for He is the Commander, the Powerful.

order.why: Link trustworthiness with justice among all peoples.
Relate character to the practice of fairness.
Make pure deeds a means for justice to appear.
shortened: God willing, may the standard of justice and the banner of wisdom be witnessed before the faces of each of you, and assuredly through these pure deeds and holy, sanctified characteristics, the lights of justice which have been veiled and concealed by the oppression of the oppressors shall shine forth through the divine name. Then shall ye see the earth transformed into another earth, and the atoms shall cry out with the most exalted call: "The horizon of justice hath been illumined by the sun of the remembrance of our Lord, the Mighty, the Manifest, the Hearing, the All-Seeing!"

order.why: Recognize benevolent effort as part of that appearance.
Connect just education with peace and renewal.
Associate religion’s social purpose with fellowship and fairness.
Give a named recipient a task of transforming discord.
shortened: O Safdar! God willing, thou wilt transform the darkness of oppression and discord in all regions into the light of justice and unity.

order.why: Make effort toward equity a continuing responsibility.
shortened: We beseech God, exalted be His glory, to confirm thee in that which shall cause the turning of souls unto Him and the unity and fellowship of hearts. God willing, rely wholly upon Him and resign thyself completely to His will, detached from all else. Strive at all times that perchance the tyranny of the world may be transformed into justice and the oppression of nations into equity.

order.why: Hold compassion and steadfast justice together.
Return to the relation between fairness and unity.
shortened: That which is the cause of the unity of the world and its peoples hath flowed forth from the Pen of the Most High in divers Tablets. God grant that all men may be adorned with the ornament of fairness and enabled to observe justice that they may partake of the fruits of what hath been mentioned and bear witness unto that which hath been ordained by the one true God, exalted be His Glory.

order.why: Retain the declaration that justice has appeared.
shortened: For years justice had been deprived and no trace of it was found. Praise be to God, in these days it hath appeared from the horizon of power with standards and banners of victory.

order.why: Imagine oppressors themselves transformed.
shortened: Ere long will God, exalted be His glory, adorn the embodiments of oppression with the raiment of justice and the temples of tyranny with the ornament of equity.

order.why: Preserve the promise of an unobscured sun of justice.
shortened: Soon will the true Omnipotent One purify the earth and cause the sun of justice to appear to all the world from behind the clouds of oppression.

order.why: Extend that light to the world.
shortened: Soon shall the Sun of Power shine forth from the horizon of God's Will and illumine the whole world with the lights of justice.

order.why: Retain the assurance of encompassing justice.
Hold present oppression and future light together.
Define the hoped-for result as security and peace for all.
shortened: The purpose of this Revelation is that the clouds of oppression may be lifted away and the Sun of Justice may shine forth from behind the veil, that all the peoples of the world may abide in the cradle of security and peace.

order.why: Make trustworthiness vivid through a traveler’s freedom from harm.
shortened: Let Me tell you that you may know: I have come so that in this world full of corruption, where the door of tranquility has been utterly shut to all beings through the oppression of the oppressors and the treachery of the treacherous, I may, by God's might and power, establish such justice, protection, trustworthiness and religion throughout all regions--manifest and resplendent--that if one of those maidens secluded behind veils, whose radiant beauty would count the sun itself as but a mote, and who in all aspects of grace and beauty would have no peer or likeness, were to emerge from behind the veil adorned with the most precious jewels and ornaments beyond the reckoning of the wise, and travel alone, unaccompanied and unhindered, from the East of creation to the West of invention, wandering through every land and journeying through every clime, such would be the trustworthiness, religiousness, justice, and fairness, and such the absence of treachery, baseness, tyranny and inequity, that no hand of aggression or greed would stretch forth toward the hem of her wealth, nor would any lustful or iniquitous eye turn to gaze upon her sanctified beauty, until she returns to her dwelling and homeland with an unsullied heart and a radiant countenance." Then He said: "By God's power, I shall transform the world in this way and shall open this most great door unto the face of all peoples." It is in reference to this that the Supreme Pen hath revealed: "Erelong shall the earth be turned into the Most Glorious Paradise."

order.why: Locate universal comfort in a particular hope for Iran.
Express the disappearance of oppression as a wish.
shortened: May no trace of oppression remain and may the beloved of justice and fairness appear resplendent.

order.why: Let knowledge and fairness become flourishing gardens.
Move into thanksgiving for justice’s light.
shortened: All praise, thanksgiving, mention, glorification, tribute and honor befit the Peerless Beloved, Who hath illumined the world of existence with the light of justice.

order.why: Pair justice and equity in praise.
Join prayer with the crown and ornament images.
shortened: We beseech God--glorified be His majesty--to adorn His servants with the ornament of justice and fairness.
Blessed is he who hath adorned his head with the crown of justice and his temple with the ornament of fairness.

order.why: Retain the prayer for just and generous hearts.
Extend that petition through a universal appeal.
Pray for justice in the earth and its thrones.
shortened: O Lord! Illumine the face of the earth with the lights of the sun of Thy justice and adorn its thrones with the temples of the dawning-places of truth and fairness, that the countenances of those who love Thee and who have believed in Thy signs may smile with joy.

order.why: Ask that tyranny’s seat become a throne of equity.
shortened: O Lord! Adorn them with the ornament of justice and equity, and illumine their hearts with the lights of bounty and grace.

I beseech Thee, O Lord of eternity and Sovereign of nations and Goal of all peoples, by Thy Most Great Name, to transform the seat of tyranny into the throne of Thy justice, and the chair of heedlessness and oppression into the seat of submission and equity.

order.why: Preserve the parallel reported prayer.
Ask that creation not be deprived of justice.
shortened: We beseech God, exalted be His glory, not to deprive His creation and to adorn them with the ornament of justice and fairness.

order.why: Connect justice with nearness.
Keep the concise universal petition.
Ask for assistance in holding fast to fairness.
End the linked sequence with guidance for a particular heart.
Retain the supplied account connecting recognition and justice.
Preserve the supplied testimony to new foundations.
Retain the supplied anticipation of full splendor.
Give communal responsibility a concrete test in protecting minorities.
Examine priority for minorities alongside equal rights.
Protect civil rights even when belief is renounced.
Close with the combined work of personal transformation, institutions and development.

questions: Which examples expose the difference between praising justice and practicing it, and where might that difference appear in ordinary relationships?
How does seeing humanity as one body change the meaning of impartiality, self-interest, and protection of vulnerable people?
What tensions and possibilities emerge when equal rights are read alongside particular attention to minorities and people who are poor or oppressed?
How would you distinguish personal generosity, mercy, public protection, and accountability across passages with different settings and authority?
What would truthful witness against oneself or one’s relatives, as in Qur’an 4:135, require of both inward habits and shared procedures?
How might changes in character, economic arrangements, and institutions reinforce one another, and which connected subject would help you examine a practical example?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 4:135 · Truthful witness beyond personal loyalty
references.note: The verse asks believers to sustain justice even when testimony goes against themselves, their parents, or relatives, and whether someone is rich or poor. Compare this demanding impartiality with the compilation’s searching eye and the ruler’s self-examination. How can affection and loyalty coexist with a refusal to distort what one knows?
